_comment: STEP A0's REGISTER — read by tools/check-scope-sites.py. Every `scopeOf(env)` call site in
worker.js must be either CONVERTED (gone) or DECLARED here with a reason. An unclassified site
is red. scopeOf() is the ONLY function that reads ESTATE_ID, so this list IS the inventory of
places that still take the household from config — converting them is the multi-tenancy flip.
KEYED BY ENCLOSING FUNCTION, NEVER BY LINE — deliberately. Three file:line citations went stale
inside single afternoons on 2026-09-12, every one from a concurrent insertion rather than a
change to the thing cited. `count` is load-bearing: it stops a declaration written today from
silently covering a site added tomorrow.
A REASON IS NOT AN AUDIT. The tool records that a human gave one; it cannot judge whether it is
good. And it reads SOURCE, NOT BEHAVIOUR — whether a converted site resolves the RIGHT grant is
step A15's falsifier at dev, and neither covers the other.
⛔ EMPTY ON PURPOSE AT A0. The plan runs the classifier BEFORE any conversion, so a full-red
first run is the intended reading: 58 sites, none yet examined. A2 converts B-CALLER, A3
converts B-CACHE, A4 DECLARES B-DEPLOY here rather than converting it.

baseline.note: the A0 inventory; `converted` is measured against this number

doorRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · A rate limit is an ABUSE control on the ORIGIN, not a household fact. Scoped per estate it would multiply: one attacker gets N x the budget by naming N households, and under one origin naming a household is free. Correct as the deployment's forever.

feedbackRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. ⚠️ It also guards the CREDENTIAL-FREE capture POST, which has no household to scope to even in principle.

probeRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. Guards /api/account/available, which is pre-account by construction — there is no estate at the moment it runs.

recoverRateLimitOk.reason: ratelimit · as doorRateLimitOk. Guards the recovery route, whose whole premise is a person who cannot reach their household; scoping its limiter to that household would be circular.

storeDoorRecord.reason: door · ⛔ A DOOR RECORD PRECEDES ANY HOUSEHOLD BY CONSTRUCTION. watch-door.py's own rule is that it reports what happened AT a door, never who was standing at it; records carry personId:null and a deviceId is a browser bucket. The reading it exists for is the SILENT case — someone arrived and neither got in nor reported a failure — and that person has no estate to file under by definition.

handleDoor.reason: door · the read side of storeDoorRecord; same scope or the channel cannot be read back.

grantFor.reason: grant (LEGACY FALLBACK) · ⛔⛔ THIS ONE IS NOT PERMANENT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SETTLED. It looks a grant up at keyFor(scopeOf(env),'grant',hash) and then rejects row.estateId !== env.ESTATE_ID, so a foreign grant fails TWICE — wrong namespace, and rejected if it were not. Both halves must change for one deployment to serve many estates, and the LOOKUP is the harder half: a token must resolve WITHOUT already knowing which estate to look in. It is declared here as the CURRENT state with its reason, not as a decision that it stays. It is step A6's object (the grant:<personId>:<estateId> edge), and it is why A3's check cannot pass before the conversion.  ⭐ SITE 2, ADDED WITH A6 (2026-09-12): storeResolveRecord(env, scopeOf(env), …) — the instrumentation for resolveByEdge()'s two non-lookup branches. It is the DEPLOYMENT's record on purpose and not the household's: the thing being counted is that this deployment could not tell WHICH of a person's houses a request meant, which is a fact about the deployment's resolver and not about either house. Filing it under one of the candidate estates would attribute an ambiguity to whichever house happened to win. ⚠️ It carries an outcome and a COUNT of candidates — never a personId, never an estateId — so nothing household-shaped is in the row to misfile. ⛔ A7 deletes the branch this records; the site goes with it.

handleAmbient.reason: cache (B-DEPLOY, DECLARED NOT CONVERTED) · stays on scopeOf because AMBIENT_MAC is a per-deployment Worker secret - the key correctly reflects deployment-wide data. ⛔ This is BY CONSTRUCTION, not by design forever: the day a household can declare its own station credential this site must be reconverted. [paul-ruled 2026-09-13, with that risk stated to him].  ⭐ THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THE RULING, so nobody re-derives it: handleAmbient reads the station MAC at `const mac = (env.AMBIENT_MAC || "").trim()` — a per-deployment Worker SECRET since 2026-09-04 (`wrangler.toml:45`), never caller-supplied. ⚠️ worker.js's own comment above the handler still says `[vars] AMBIENT_MAC` from C5 7c (2026-09-03) — that is one day stale and the binding moved to a secret; the RULING rests on per-deployment, which both eras satisfy. The cache key's household-identifying suffix is therefore the DEPLOYMENT's own station, so the key is already exactly as specific as the data behind it. Gating the route would not change that, and converting it would make the key ASSERT a per-household scoping the data does not have — a key that claims more than it knows. ⚠️ It is the one site in this register whose reason is about the DATA rather than about the caller: the other three B-CACHE sites (airnow · drought · today-line) converted at A3 because their suffix is the CALLER's coordinates, county and canon. ⛔ The separate question — SHOULD /api/ambient be gated at all (it is deliberately ungated since 2026-08-02 so Mom's unpaired devices keep working) — is untouched by this ruling and stays open.

handleChat.reason: chat-budget · a daily model-spend CEILING is a deployment-wide control. Per-estate budget keys would give every household its own ceiling, so the origin's total spend would become unbounded in the number of households — the opposite of what a ceiling is for.

handleEstateFound.reason: account (LEGACY SHAPE) · putAccount(env, scopeOf(env), …) — the scope reaches ONLY accountKey(scope, username), the username-keyed legacy row. The AUTHORITATIVE account row is account:<personId> and takes no scope at all. ⭐ C7 [paul-ruled 2026-09-10]: AN ACCOUNT BELONGS TO A PERSON, NOT TO A HOUSEHOLD — 'we shouldn't be pre-seeding estates earlier in the process'. The hierarchy is person → account → estate, so an account key carrying an estate prefix cannot express the thing it is keying. Scoping this to the founded estate would be the DEFECT, not the fix. ⚠️ This is the register's one row that is deployment-scoped because the DATA IS NOT A HOUSEHOLD'S, as distinct from the ratelimit rows (a control on the origin) and handleAmbient (data that is the deployment's). Three different reasons that look alike from a distance.

fetch(dispatcher).reason: ⛔⛔ ELEVEN SITES IN FOUR CLASSES, ENUMERATED — NOT ONE REASON STRETCHED OVER ELEVEN. The register's own note warned that a single declaration here would cover sites that 'do not share one' reason; the answer is a reason that ENUMERATES rather than one that generalises. Sites are named by their ROUTE, never by line — three file:line citations went stale inside single afternoons on 2026-09-12. Classified 2026-09-13, AFTER the door steps (A6/A9/A11/A13) landed, which is the sequence the note demanded: classifying a site inside a block those steps were about to rewrite would have been a guess about code that did not exist.  ① ACCOUNT / SESSION — THE LEGACY USERNAME-KEYED SHAPE (7): POST /api/account (handleAccountCreate) · POST /api/profile's `sc` · GET /api/account/available (accountFor) · /api/account/username (handleUsernameChange) · /api/session (handleSession) · and /api/grant/whoami's TWO accountKey(scopeOf(env), grant.username) reads. Every one reaches only accountKey/accountFor/putAccount. ⭐ C7 [paul-ruled 2026-09-10] — an account belongs to a PERSON, not a household; the authoritative row is account:<personId> and takes no scope. VERIFIED BY READING EACH: handleAccountCreate uses scope at exactly two lines (accountKey, accountFor); handleUsernameChange at one (fromKey/toKey); handleSession at one (accountFor), deriving the ESTATE separately from the route via scopeOfRoute. ⚠️ POST /api/profile's `sc` was MIXED until 2026-09-13 — it also fed applyGeocode, which is a household fact — and was SPLIT rather than declared over. A declaration that had covered it would have been false about half of what the site did.  ② ABUSE CONTROLS ON THE ORIGIN (2): /health's chat-budget read (dateKey · chat-budget) and /api/onboarding-metrics' obmetrics ratelimit bucket. Same reasons already carried by handleChat and doorRateLimitOk: a per-estate ceiling makes the origin's total spend unbounded in the number of households, and a per-estate limiter hands an attacker N× the budget for naming N houses.  ③ THE RECOVERY RECORD (1): /api/recovery's dateKey(scopeOf(env), 'recovery', …). ⭐ The channel's whole premise is A PERSON WHO CANNOT REACH THEIR HOUSEHOLD, so filing their request under the household they cannot reach is circular — the same reasoning recoverRateLimitOk already carries, applied to the record rather than the limiter. B6r [paul-ruled 2026-09-11]: its own key, its own ADMIN-ONLY reader. ⚠️ A signed-in caller's request IS attributable and this still files it at the deployment; that is deliberate (one channel, one reader) and is the weakest reason in this row.  ④ ONBOARDING TELEMETRY (1): /api/onboarding-metrics' dateKey. It records what happened AT A DOOR before any household exists — the same construction as storeDoorRecord, already declared: records carry no personId and a deviceId is a browser bucket.  ⛔ WHAT THIS DECLARATION CANNOT DO, on its own face: the `count` clause catches a NEW site appearing in the dispatcher (12 found against 11 declared is red), but nothing catches an EXISTING site CHANGING CLASS. If a route in ① ever keys a household fact from this scope, this register will still read green. That is the same blind spot as `assertScope`'s — it sees a missing conversion, never a wrong one — and it is why A15's falsifier at two estates is not optional.

_declared_note: ⛔ DECLARED means: this site STAYS on scopeOf(env) BY DESIGN. It does NOT mean 'not yet converted'.
A site awaiting a later slice must stay UNCLASSIFIED — declaring it would launder PENDING into
BY DESIGN, the instrument would read green, and the pass that owed the work would skip it because
the tool said it was handled. That is 'an unchecked box is not open work' inverted into its more
dangerous direction: marking open work CLOSED.
⚠️ `grantFor` is the one row here that is NOT permanent, and it says so in its own reason.
_unclassified_note: ✅ ZERO UNCLASSIFIED as of 2026-09-13 (the writers' slice). This note described 24, then 20, and is
kept — rewritten — rather than deleted, because WHAT MOVED is the useful part.
⭐ THE WRITERS' SLICE `[paul-ruled 2026-09-13]`. A14's gate demands 0 unclassified and row A could not
reach it: four sites carried a forward reference to 'the writers' slice' and THE BUILD PLAN NEVER
CONTAINED ONE (measured: the word 'writers' appears zero times in it). Paul ruled the GATE right and
the ROW's scope incomplete — writes must convert before row B opens regardless of which row they are
filed under, because at the production origin a write from any household would land under the
deployment's own estate while READS resolved per household. Silent, and in the dangerous direction.
CONVERTED HERE (8): handleZoneAudio (4) · handleFeedback (2) · /api/grant/whoami's geocode retry and
its grant-row write (2). Plus one site SPLIT rather than declared: POST /api/profile's account-branch
geocode, which shared a `scopeOf(env)` with the legacy account key and needed a different answer.
⛔⛔ THE PRE-AUTH CAPTURE PARAGRAPH THAT USED TO SIT HERE WAS WRONG ABOUT SIX OF ITS SEVEN SITES, and
that is worth more than the correction. It recorded handleFeedback (2) and handleZoneAudio (4) as
'UNATTRIBUTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — they run BEFORE a grant exists'. Both functions RESOLVE A GRANT:
handleZoneAudio does it on its own first line; handleFeedback is handed one by the dispatcher and
`feedbackDestination(grant, …)` reads it to decide the destination. So the claim was checkable and
false, and it had already been CAUGHT ONCE: the 2026-09-11 stage-note in the build plan (line 127)
says GET /api/feedback 'use[s] dateKey(scopeOf(env)) not scopeFor(request) (TIER 1 · 54)' and folds
it into A2 `[paul-ruled]`. A2 closed without it, and this register then re-recorded the same site as
correct-by-construction. ⭐ A WRONG REASON IS WORSE THAN NO REASON: an unclassified site gets looked
at again, and a declared one does not.
⚠️ WHAT REMAINS TRUE OF CREDENTIAL-FREE CAPTURE, and it is a real residue rather than a fixed thing:
a capture arriving with NO credential still falls back to the deployment's estate, so at a deployment
holding several households no household can read it back as theirs. `scopeFor` makes the credentialled
case right and leaves that one exactly as honest as it was. Measured 2026-09-12: credential-free
capture is a LEGACY-ONLY affordance (legacy 11/11; home 0/17), so nothing is stranded today.
⛔ AND THE STANDING WARNING, unchanged: a site awaiting a later slice must stay UNCLASSIFIED.
Declaring it launders PENDING into BY DESIGN, the instrument reads green, and the pass that owed the
work skips it because the tool said it was handled.
